headline: MacIntyre's command puts Tennessee in firm control over Georgia
body: Tennessee's offense moved with surgical precision on Saturday, dismantling Georgia 43-7 in a Week 10 statement game that left little doubt about which team came prepared. George MacIntyre orchestrated the attack with composure, completing 24 of 32 passes for 343 yards and a touchdown while managing the game without a turnover. The Volunteers' balanced attack—153 rushing yards supported by that efficient passing game—created constant pressure that Georgia's defense simply could not answer.

Georgia's defensive unit, led by Wolf's eight tackles, worked hard but faced the impossible task of stopping an opponent that didn't beat itself. The Bulldogs' offense managed only 150 passing yards and 60 on the ground, never finding rhythm against Tennessee's defense. Quarterback Giles did what he could with limited opportunities, throwing for 161 yards and a touchdown, but the game's trajectory was set early and never shifted.

The separation in total yardage—Tennessee's 489 to Georgia's 210—tells the real story. Tennessee controlled line of scrimmage in both directions, a foundation that made MacIntyre's job far easier. This was less about one team's brilliance and more about Tennessee executing a complete game while Georgia couldn't generate the offensive spark needed to stay competitive.
turningPoint: Tennessee scored on three of its first four drives, establishing a 21-0 lead that forced Georgia into constant catch-up mode and prevented the Bulldogs from ever threatening an upset.

unsungHero.name: Bishop
unsungHero.why: While MacIntyre rightly earned Player of the Game, Bishop's 10 carries for 78 yards provided the ground presence that kept Georgia's defense honest and opened up the passing lanes that MacIntyre exploited all afternoon.
